title: Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
summary: Score centering replaces (or complements) importance-sampling corrections for training-inference mismatch in RL post-training of LLMs by adding an additive drift-canceling term to the score rather than reweighting samples. It costs little compute or memory since the correction is additive, but adds implementation complexity in the RL training loop and requires a reliable estimate of the persistent bias between engines. It can fail if the mismatch is not primarily drift (e.g., high-variance noise rather than persistent bias), if the drift estimate itself is noisy or unstable, or in setups where training and inference engines can simply be kept consistent.
rationale: The reader may run RL post-training on a single GPU with quantized inference rollouts, where this low-cost additive correction is worth small-scale validation before replacing importance-sampling machinery.
technique: Score centering for RL training-inference mismatch

claims.statement: Score centering replaces (or complements) importance-sampling corrections for training-inference mismatch in RL post-training of LLMs by adding an additive drift-canceling term to the score rather than reweighting samples. It costs little compute or memory since the correction is additive, but adds implementation complexity in the RL training loop and requires a reliable estimate of the persistent bias between engines. It can fail if the mismatch is not primarily drift (e.g., high-variance noise rather than persistent bias), if the drift estimate itself is noisy or unstable, or in setups where training and inference engines can simply be kept consistent.

Score centering alone matches or outperforms importance-sampling-based methods under quantization-induced mismatch, with the gap growing as mismatch worsens; composing it with importance sampling outperforms pure importance-sampling baselines under staleness.
